title: POC scoping: open-model shortlist + multilingual tradeoffs - Cygnus Thera
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria for a multilingual medical summarization POC. Discussed target latency (<= 700ms for short queries, <= 2.5s for long summaries), target throughput (approx 25 qps sustained), dataset size and anonymization constraints, shortlist of open models to evaluate (Mistral, Llama-2 variants, Falcon, Mosaic models), and benchmarking plan over a 4-week sprint with hardware and metrics. Action items include sharing benchmark sheet, Redwood security pack, and scheduling a week-1 baseline run.
action_items: Maya Chen | Share benchmark spreadsheet and POC template | 2026-05-01
Priya Patel | Provision test endpoints on Redwood hosted sandbox and sample config | 2026-05-04
Arman Kaur | Provide 200 de-identified documents per language (en/es/fr/de) and success rubric | 2026-05-05
Sofia Mendes | Supply 50 localization edge-case prompts and examples | 2026-05-05
Liam O'Connor | Confirm network/VPC requirements and preferred KMS provider | 2026-05-07
next_steps: Redwood to send POC contract and sandbox access
Customer to prepare dataset and rubric
Schedule baseline benchmark run (week 1) and weekly syncs (Tuesdays)
Plan for dedicated instance sizing if baseline meets quality thresholds
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro: I'm Maya, AE on this account, with Diego and Priya from the solutions team. how's everyone's audio?
[00:08] Arman Kaur: good, thanks. arman here. excited to get into the model tradeoffs.
[00:12] Sofia Mendes: Sofia, hi, Localization lead — we'll be focused on Spanish and Portuguese and also French later.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Liam - platform eng. i'll handle infra questions.
[00:20] Diego Ramos: great. goal for today is to align on success criteria, narrow an open-model shortlist, and agree a bench and timeline. We'll also flag security/ops constraints.
[00:31] Maya Chen: quick housekeep — call will be recorded, we'll share notes. does anyone need to add stakeholders?
[00:36] Arman Kaur: we'll loop in legal later but not on this call.
[00:40] Priya Patel: ok, jumping in on workload sizing: Arman, can you describe typical prompt size and cardinality?
[00:46] Arman Kaur: sure. most requests are 1-2 paragraph clinical encounter notes — 200 to 800 tokens typically. For summarization we expect output 50-150 tokens for short summaries, and up to 600 tokens for case syntheses. Volume: current peak is ~15 qps across EU+US, expected growth. For POC, emulate 20-30 qps sustained.
[01:10] Diego Ramos: that helps. latency target? what do you need for the UI flows?
[01:14] Sofia Mendes: For short summaries we want interactive feel, ideally sub-second, let's say 600-700 ms median. For full case syntheses up to 2.5s is OK. when you scale to 600 token outputs, obviously it's longer.
[01:29] Priya Patel: noted. question about multilingual: which languages matter and do you have parallel data?
[01:33] Sofia Mendes: English and Spanish are highest. Portuguese and French are medium. We have some parallel de-identified notes, but limited. we can create 200 docs per lang for POC.
[01:44] Maya Chen: good. on models — we usually recommend evaluating a small shortlist to test quality/latency tradeoffs. Diego, want to run through options?
[01:50] Diego Ramos: sure. Open-ish shortlist we suggest: 1) Mistral medium/large (strong for reasoning/short form), 2) Llama-2 13B and 70B variants, 3) Falcon-40B, 4) MosaicML's MPT-30B or their newer mosaic family. Also consider quantized variants — 8-bit and 4-bit — for cost. Each has different multilingual and domain behavior.
[02:16] Arman Kaur: quick interjection — we've seen Llama-2 sometimes hallucinate in clinical contexts. are any of these better at factuality?
[02:23] Diego Ramos: factuality is model-specific and depends on prompt engineering and evals. shorter responses and stricter instruction tuning help. Mistral tends to be crisp but can be optimistic. Falcon has decent base performance but sometimes lacks in non-English. We should test on your rubric.
[02:40] Sofia Mendes: How about latency on hosted vs dedicated? we might need private deployment because of PHI concerns.
[02:45] Priya Patel: yes — PHI triggers stricter controls. Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is available; we can run the POC either on Redwood Hosted sandbox with encrypted rest endpoints where data is transient, or on a private VPC if you need to keep data in your network. There will be different lead times.
[03:03] Liam O'Connor: if we go private, we need KMS integration and audit logs — SOC2 is baseline for us. What's Redwood's current attestation?
[03:12] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC 2 and ISO documents — we'll attach the security pack. We support external KMS providers and have audit log options.
[03:20] Arman Kaur: great. back to model shortlist — can we add a distilled/quantized Llama-2 13B to test the cost sweet-spot?
[03:27] Diego Ramos: absolutely. practical approach: baseline with FP16 Llama-2 70B and 13B, and quantized 13B (4-bit) and Mistral-Std. Also include Falcon-40B. If network and infra permit, we can include a Mosaic latest too. That gives variety across size and architecture.
[03:48] Sofia Mendes: for multilingual quality, are there known wins? Llama variants have improved Spanish but sometimes degrade scientific/medical terms.
[03:56] Diego Ramos: yeah. Mistral seems strong in ES/FR for conversational and summarization, but domain-specific terms need evals. Mosaic and Falcon sometimes underperform on Portuguese. We'll instrument BLEU/ROUGE and a manual clinical-accuracy check.
[04:10] Priya Patel: on benchmarks — recommend three tiers: perf (latency/throughput), quality (ROUGE/BERTScore/clinical accuracy judgement), and robustness (edge-case prompts and hallucination rate). We'll need to decide thresholds for "pass".
[04:22] Arman Kaur: for success criteria, propose: 1) human-rated clinical accuracy >= 85% on short summaries, 2) median latency <= 700ms for 100-token outputs, 3) hallucination rate <= 5% on clinical anchors, 4) cost per 1k tokens under $X (we need Redwood estimate).
[04:41] Maya Chen: that's good. we'll model cost once we know quantization and batching rules. Priya, Diego — can you estimate host vs dedicated delta?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: quick rough: hosted sandbox (shared) will have higher variance but lower ops overhead. For sustained 25 qps on 200-token avg outputs, you probably need 2-3 GPU instances dedicated (A100-class) or a single larger pool with batching; dedicated reserved will give better p99 latency and predictable cost. Quantized 4-bit on A10G or H100 improves throughput. We'll put numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: what about KV cache misinterpreted as K-V cash in transcription — joking — but serious: are we able to reuse context caches between very similar prompts?
[05:20] Priya Patel: Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching and we can apply prefix reuse for repeated passages to cut token compute. We'll add config for cache TTLs.
[05:29] Sofia Mendes: for bilingual prompts, sometimes the model switches register. We'll include localization testcases.
[05:34] Diego Ramos: please send those testcases. We'll include a language breakdown in the bench.
[05:38] Maya Chen: timeline thoughts — we typically run a 4-week POC: week 0 prep (data & infra), week 1 baseline runs, week 2-3 iterative tuning and targeted evals, week 4 final validation and go/no-go. Does that align?
[05:52] Arman Kaur: yes, 4-week is reasonable. Legal may push for a short pilot clause though.
[05:57] Maya Chen: understood. we'll draft the POC SOW and share.
[06:01] Diego Ramos: on benchmarks — we need to capture tokenization mismatches across tokenizers (some models use different BPEs), that affects cost. We'll normalize by UTF-8 token estimates and measure raw tokens passed.
[06:15] Arman Kaur: ok. on evaluation, clinical accuracy judgement — who on your side will do the human ratings?
[06:20] Sofia Mendes: our clinical reviewers will sample 200 summaries per language, but we may need to augment with Redwood's eval tooling.
[06:26] Priya Patel: we can onboard them to Redwood Console evals and set up labeling tasks.
[06:31] Liam O'Connor: about private deployment lead times — what's typical? weeks?
[06:34] Maya Chen: for VPC deployments with KMS and audit config, typical lead is 3-4 weeks depending on contracts. Hosted POC is faster — 2-3 days for sandbox access.
[06:45] Arman Kaur: contract lead time likely. Can we start with hosted baseline and then replicate on private infra if quality warrants it?
[06:52] Diego Ramos: that's a good pattern. do baseline on hosted to iterate quickly, then replicate on dedicated/private for final benchmark.
[06:58] Sofia Mendes: any advice on prompt templates for clinical summarization?
[07:02] Priya Patel: keep instructions explicit, include anchors to patient-safe facts, and include a refusal style for unsupported claims. We'll share templates.
[07:09] Arman Kaur: hallucination mitigation is biggest worry. Also redaction / PII handling.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Redwood has PII redaction patterns and we can run pipeline pre-processing to strip identifiers. We'll include that in the POC plan.
[07:22] Diego Ramos: quick note on quantization quality: 4-bit quant can degrade some rarer token probabilities and that can matter for clinical terms. So for any 4-bit candidate we should run clinical-term recall tests.
[07:34] Sofia Mendes: that's critical. add it to the bench.
[07:37] Maya Chen: moving to explicit bench metrics: we'll record median and p95 latency per model and per output length bucket (100t, 300t, 600t); throughput at target concurrency; ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a custom clinical-accuracy score, plus hallucination % and token-cost. sound right?
[07:55] Arman Kaur: yep. also track failure modes and truncation rates.
[07:59] Priya Patel: we'll collect logs and show dashboards in Redwood Console, per-route breakdown.
[08:03] Liam O'Connor: from infra perspective, if we parallelize across regions (EU/US) we'll need geo routing and consistent model versions; does Redwood handle model pinning?
[08:12] Diego Ramos: yes, model pinning and rollout policies are supported. You can pin a route to a specific model variant and rollout progressively.
[08:19] Maya Chen: next steps recap — Maya to share security pack and SOW; Priya to provision sandbox; Diego to emit benchmark spreadsheet and sample configs; Arman/Sofia to supply datasets and rubrics; Liam to confirm KMS details.
[08:32] Sofia Mendes: one more question — competitor options we considered internally: Anthropic Claude for safety but closed, Cohere for embeddings and some generation; but we want open-model control.
[08:42] Maya Chen: good note. open models give you adjustability and lower lock-in risk.
[08:46] Arman Kaur: last one — any initial cost ballpark for 4-week POC with hosted runs and 2 weeks of heavier load?
[08:52] Diego Ramos: rough guestimate: hosted sandbox runs are low — under $3k for baseline. Full evaluation with multiple model variants and quantization runs could be $8-12k. Dedicated or private will be higher — we'll provide a formal estimate in the spreadsheet.
[09:05] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll share docs and schedule the baseline. thanks everyone.
[09:09] Arman Kaur: thanks.
[09:11] Sofia Mendes: thanks all.
[09:13] Liam O'Connor: bye.
[09:15] [call ends]
